Function backparse3(s:seq.symbol, ii:int, includeDefine:boolean) int /rmbr let i = if true then addDefine(s, ii) else ii /rmbr assert i > 0 report" back parse 1a: :(s):(stacktrace)" /rmbr let kind = kind.s sub i, /rmbr if kind = kendblock then matchblock(s, i - 1, 0) /rmbr else let i1 = if kind = kjmp then i - value.s sub i /rmbr else i for k = i1 /rmbr, j ∈ constantseq( nopara.s sub i1, 1) do backparse3(s, k - 1, includeDefine), /rmbr if includeDefine then addDefine(s, k) else k

function matchblock(s:seq.symbol, i:int, nest:int) int /rmbr let sym = s sub i /rmbr let kind = kind.sym /rmbr let newnest = if kind ∈ [ kloop, kstart] then nest - 1 /rmbr else if kind = kendblock then nest + 1 /rmbr else nest, if nest = 0 then if kind = kloop then for k = i /rmbr, j ∈ constantseq( nopara.sym, 1) do backparse3(s, k - 1, false), /rmbr k else if kind = kstart then addDefine(s, i) /rmbr else matchblock(s, i - 1, newnest) else matchblock(s, i - 1, newnest)

function addDefine(s:seq.symbol, i:int) int /rmbr if i > 1 /rmbr ∧ kind.s sub (i - 1)/rmbr = kdefine then addDefine(s, backparse3(s, i - 2, false))/rmbr else i

Function towords(s:seq.token) seq.word /rmbr for acc = "" , e ∈ s do acc + toword.e, /rmbr acc

function =(a:tkn, b:tkn) boolean w.a = w.b

Function addprec(str:seq.word, internal:boolean) seq.word /rmbr{ ???? no need for internal? } /rmbr for precedence = 0, e ∈ str /rmbr do if e ∈ " for " then precedence /rmbr else if e ∈ " precedence " then -1 /rmbr else if precedence < 0 then if e ∈ " 1 3 4 5 6 7 20 30 31 32 33 34 35 36 37 11 " then toint.e /rmbr else let prec = opprec.e /rmbr assert prec ∈ [1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7] report":(e) does not have a precedence " , /rmbr prec else assert eqvclass.token. decode. encode.tkn(e, token(e, precedence))/rmbr = precedence report":(e) has already been given a different precedence: /br :(str)" , /rmbr precedence,""

Function tknencoding seq.word /rmbr let str = " precedence 20 Function function precedence 1 sub sup precedence 3 for * / >> << mod ∩ ∪ \ precedence 4+-∈ ∉ precedence 5 = > < ≠ ≥ ≤ precedence 6 ∧ precedence 7 ∨ ⊻ precedence 11 $mergecode precedence 30, precedence 31.precedence 32: " /rmbr + " precedence 33(precedence 34)precedence 35[precedence 36]precedence 37 " /rmbr + dq sub 1, addprec(str + " precedence+for ∈ ∉ " , true)

function finishmodule(/rmbr modtext0:seq.seq.word /rmbr, reorguse:boolean /rmbr, bind:boolean /rmbr, m:midpoint /rmbr, modrenames:seq.word /rmbr) seq.seq.word /rmbr let modname = (modtext0 sub 1) sub 2 /rmbr for modtext = empty:seq.seq.word /rmbr, uses = empty:seq.seq.word /rmbr, ingenerated = false /rmbr, p ∈ modtext0 do if ingenerated then next(modtext + p, uses, true) /rmbr else if p = " <<<< Below is auto generated code >>>> " then next(modtext + p, uses, true) /rmbr else if p sub 1 /rmbr ∈ " Function function Export unbound Builtin builtin precedence type " then next(modtext + pretty.p, uses, ingenerated)/rmbr else if getkey.p ∈ " use " ∧ reorguse then next(modtext, uses + p << 1, ingenerated)/rmbr else next(modtext + p, uses, ingenerated) let uselist0 = if bind ∧ reorguse then for dict = empty:set.symbol, sd ∈ toseq.prg.m /rmbr do dict + sym.sd /rmbr for uselist = empty:seq.seq.word /rmbr, ref4 ∈ toseq. reconstruceUses(m, modname, dict, exportedmodref.m, uses) do uselist + %.ref4, /rmbr uselist else uses for uselist1 = empty:seq.seq.word, u ∈ uselist0 /rmbr do assert not. isempty.u report" SDF " /rmbr{ only first word of u is a module name } /rmbr uselist1 /rmbr + ([ rename(modrenames, u sub 1)]/rmbr + u << 1) for idx = 0, e ∈ modtext /rmbr while getkey.e ∈ " precedence noncode Module " /rmbr do idx + 1 /rmbr for newuses = empty:seq.seq.word /rmbr, e ∈ sortuse(uselist1, "" ) do newuses + [ " use :(e)" ], /rmbr subseq(modtext, 1, idx)/rmbr + newuses /rmbr + modtext << idx

function TOC(input:seq.seq.word, html:seq.word) seq.seq.word /rmbr let h = " /h1 /h2 /h3 /h4 /h5 /h6 " /rmbr let Module = -1 /rmbr for kinds = empty:set.int, e ∈ html /rmbr do let a = findindex( " h1 h2 h3 h4 h5 h6 " , e), /rmbr if a > n.h then if e ∈ " Module " then kinds + Module else kinds else kinds + a, if isempty.kinds then input /rmbr else for acc = empty:seq.seq.word, toc = "" , count = 1, lasth = 1, lastmod = 0, p ∈ input /rmbr do let kind = if n.p < 2 then n.h + 2 /rmbr else if p sub 1 ∈ " Module " then Module /rmbr else let t = findindex(h, last.p), /rmbr if t ≤ n.h then t else n.h + 2, if kind > n.h ∨ kind ∉ kinds then next(acc + p, toc, count, lasth, lastmod)/rmbr else let tagname = if kind = Module then p sub 2 else toword.count let href = " // :( merge( " # " + tagname)) /href " , /rmbr if kind = Module then let newacc = acc + p, /rmbr next(newacc, toc + " // :(href):(p) /a " , count + 1, lasth, 1) else next( acc /rmbr + " // // :(tagname) /id :(p >> 1):( last.p)" /rmbr, toc /rmbr + levelchange(kind - (lastmod + lasth))/rmbr + " // :(href):(p >> 1) /a " /rmbr, count + 1 /rmbr, kind /rmbr, 0),[toc + levelchange(1 - (lastmod + lasth))]/rmbr + acc

" Head Export type:any Type' /action Export type:$.1 $.2 /br :( $$) / any any:any Type' FPL any Type' /action $.1 $.2:$.3 $.4 $.5 $.6 $.7 /br :( $$) / any any FPL any Type' /action $.1 $.2 $.3 $.4 $.5 /br :( $$) * Type'.any /action /All /br :( $$) FPL(L)/action($.1)/br :( $$) / /action /br :( $$) * L !)any /action /All " , run(gram, s) << 1

function cleanExport(a:seq.word) seq.word /rmbr{ removes parameter names and comments } /rmbr for acc = "" , inpara = false, w ∈ a /rmbr while w ∉ " { " /rmbr do if w ∈ " ( " then next(acc + w, true) /rmbr else if w ∈ " ) " then next(acc + w, false) /rmbr else if inpara ∧ w ∈ " : " then next(acc >> 1, inpara) /rmbr else next(acc + w, inpara), acc

function cleanExports(m:midpoint) seq.seq.word /rmbr for acc3 = empty:set.exportinfo /rmbr, modname2 = " ? " sub 1 /rmbr, p ∈ src.m do{ this loop finds constructors for types } /rmbr if p sub 1 ∈ " Module module " then next(acc3, p sub 2) /rmbr else if p sub 1 ∈ " type " then next( acc3 /rmbr + exportinfo( modname2 /rmbr, " Export :(p sub 2) ( :(p << 3) ) :(p sub 2):(( if " T " sub 1 ∈ p then " .T " else"" ))" )/rmbr, modname2) else next(acc3, modname2) for acc = acc3, m1 ∈ libmods.m /rmbr do{ this loop finds symbols exported from modules } /rmbr for acc2 = acc, sym ∈ exports.m1 /rmbr do let t = getSymdef(prg.m, sym)/rmbr let symdef = if isempty.t /rmbr ∨ paragraphno.t sub 1 = 0 then if istype.sym then" Export type: :( resulttype.sym)" /rmbr else let tmp = %.sym, /rmbr" Export :(tmp << findindex(tmp, " : " sub 1))" else getHeader.(src.m) sub paragraphno.t sub 1, if name.modname.m1 = name.module.sym /rmbr ∧ subseq(symdef, 1, 1) = " Function " then acc2 /rmbr else{ cannot easily identify what module"Builtin"was exported from } /rmbr let from = if name.modname.m1 = name.module.sym /rmbr ∨ name.module.sym ∈ " builtin internal " then"" /rmbr else" {From :(module.sym) } " , acc2 /rmbr + exportinfo(name.modname.m1, " Export :(symdef << 1):(from)" ), acc2 for src2 = empty:seq.seq.word, modname = " ? " sub 1, p ∈ src.m /rmbr do if p sub 1 ∈ " Module module " then next(src2 + p, p sub 2)/rmbr else if p sub 1 ∈ " Export " then let match = lookup(acc, exportinfo(modname, p))/rmbr let toadd = if n.match ≠ 1 then{ for txt ="", e ∈ toseq.findelement2(acc, exportinfo(modname,""))do txt+%(cleanExport.p = cleanExport.exporttxt.e)+%.e assert false report"NOMTC"+cleanExport.p+"/p /rmbr "+txt,} /rmbr p /rmbr + " {no match} " else let new = exporttxt.match sub 1 /rmbr let j = findindex(p, " { " sub 1), /rmbr if j > n.p /rmbr ∨ subseq(p, j + 1, j + 1)/rmbr = " From " then new /rmbr else let extractedComment = subseq(p, j, j + findindex(p << j, " { " sub 1) - 1) let k = findindex(new, " { " sub 1), /rmbr subseq(new, 1, k - 1)/rmbr + extractedComment /rmbr + subseq(new, k, n.p), next(src2 + toadd, modname) else next(src2 + p, modname), src2

function getkey(p:seq.word) word /rmbr let keyidx = findindex(p, " /keyword " sub 1)/rmbr let key2 = if keyidx > n.p /rmbr ∨ p sub 1 ∉ " // " then p sub 1 /rmbr else p sub (keyidx - 1), if key2 ∈ " Function function Builtin builtin Export Module unbound Unbound precedence type use " then key2 /rmbr else" noncode " sub 1

Function transform2(/rmbr m:midpoint /rmbr, output:seq.word /rmbr, target:seq.word /rmbr, modrenames:seq.word /rmbr, bind:boolean /rmbr, reorguse:boolean /rmbr, html:seq.word /rmbr, cleanexports:boolean /rmbr, moveexports:boolean /rmbr, input2:seq.file /rmbr, link:seq.file /rmbr, patternmods:seq.word /rmbr) seq.file /rmbr{ let testW = n.input2 = 1 ∧ name.fn.input2 sub 1 ∈"symbolconstant" } /rmbr{ ???? moveexport not implemented, Detection of duplicate Exports } /rmbr let patterns = if not.bind /rmbr ∨ isempty.patternmods then empty:seq.patternType /rmbr else getpatterns(m, patternmods) let srctext0 = if bind then let changed = changes(m, patterns)/rmbr let prg = if isempty.changed then toseq.prg.m /rmbr else toseq( asset.changed ∪ prg.m) let src = if cleanexports then cleanExports.m /rmbr else src.m let autolinks = if not. isempty.link then getautolinks(m, link)/rmbr else empty:set.autolink, for lastno = 0, acc5 = empty:seq.seq.word, sd ∈ sort>4.prg /rmbr do if paragraphno.sd = 0 then next(lastno, acc5) /rmbr else let srctext2 = src sub paragraphno.sd, /rmbr if srctext2 sub 1 ∈ " Function function Builtin builtin " then let tmp0 = prettyFunction(srctext2, code.sd, autolinks)/rmbr + " /code " , next( paragraphno.sd /rmbr, acc5 /rmbr + subseq(src, lastno + 1, paragraphno.sd - 1)/rmbr + tmp0) else next(lastno, acc5), acc5 + subseq(src, lastno + 1, n.src) else let discard = tknencoding /rmbr for acc = empty:seq.seq.word, i ∈ input2 /rmbr do if ext.fn.i ∈ " libinfo " then acc /rmbr else let prgrph = breakparagraph. data.i for acc1 = acc, skip = false, p ∈ prgrph /rmbr do let key = p sub 1, /rmbr if key ∈ " Module module " then next(acc1 + p, false) /rmbr else if skip then next(acc1, skip) /rmbr else if n.p > 3 /rmbr ∧ key ∈ " precedence " /rmbr ∧ p sub 3 ∈ " for " then let discard1 = addprec(p, false), /rmbr next(acc1 + p, skip) else if key ∈ " Function function Builtin builtin " then if subseq(p, 1, 2)/rmbr ∈ [ " function genPEG " , " function genEnum " ]/rmbr ∧ isempty.html then for new = empty:seq.seq.word /rmbr, pp ∈ if p sub 2 ∈ " genEnum " then generateEnum.p /rmbr else generatePEG.p do new /rmbr + ( if pp sub 1 ∈ " Function function builtin Builtin type Export " then pretty.pp /rmbr else pp), next( acc1 /rmbr + [ pretty.p, " <<<< Below is auto generated code >>>> " ]/rmbr + new /rmbr + [ " Module auto gen end " ]/rmbr, true) else let tmp = pretty.p /rmbr{ for id ="", e ∈ tmp while e ∉"/id"do if e ∈"//"then""else id+e assert false report"ids"+id+showZ.subseq(tmp, 1, 20) } /rmbr next(acc1 + tmp, skip) else next(acc1 + p, skip), acc1, acc let srctext = { create table of content } TOC(srctext0, html) let directory = if isempty.target then " tmp " else target{ break into modules } /rmbr let inModule = 1 /rmbr let skip = 2 /rmbr for modinfo = empty:seq.modinfo /rmbr, modText = empty:seq.seq.word /rmbr, lib2 = directory sub 1 /rmbr, mod2dir = "" /rmbr, state = 0 /rmbr, p ∈ srctext + " Module ? " do if isempty.p /rmbr ∨ subseq(p, 1, 2) = " # File " ∧ n.p > 5 then next(modinfo, modText, merge(directory + " / " + p sub 5), mod2dir, state)/rmbr else if p = " Module auto gen end " then next(modinfo, modText, lib2, mod2dir, skip) /rmbr else let key = getkey.p, /rmbr if key ∈ " Module module " then if state = 0 then{ first module } /rmbr let newmodinfo = if isempty.modText then modinfo /rmbr else[modinfo( "" , modText)], next(newmodinfo, [p], lib2, [lib2], inModule) else let modname = rename(modrenames, (modText sub 1) sub 2)/rmbr let newModText = [ " // // :(modname) /id Module /keyword " + modname + modText sub 1 << 2]/rmbr + modText << 1, let newway0 = finishmodule(newModText, reorguse, bind, m, modrenames), /rmbr next( modinfo + modinfo(mod2dir + modname, newway0)/rmbr, [p]/rmbr, lib2 /rmbr, [lib2]/rmbr, inModule) else if state = skip then next(modinfo, modText + p, lib2, mod2dir, state) /rmbr else next(modinfo, modText + p, lib2, mod2dir, state) { Create the output files. One sfile is created if producing HTML output. Otherwise, a file is created for each Module. } /rmbr if not. isempty.html then for maintxt = "" , e ∈ modinfo do maintxt + %( " /p " , body.e), /rmbr[ file( filename.output, maintxt)] else let bindpara = if not.bind then "" /rmbr else" bind :(/rmbr( if isempty.patterns then "" /rmbr else" patterns applied: :(patterns)" )/rmbr)" let para = ( if reorguse then " reorguse " else"" )/rmbr + bindpara /rmbr + ( if cleanexports then " cleanexports " else"" )/rmbr + for txt2 = "" , x ∈ input2 /rmbr do txt2 + " /br " + fullname.fn.x, /rmbr txt2, for files = empty:seq.file, summary = " inputs :(para) /p files created " , e ∈ modinfo /rmbr do if isempty.filename.e then next(files, summary) /rmbr else let fn = filename. " + :(filename.e) .ls " /rmbr for newway = empty:seq.seq.word, e2 ∈ body.e /rmbr do newway + removeMarkup.e2, /rmbr next( files + file(fn, %( " /p " , newway) >> 1)/rmbr, summary + " /br " + fullname.fn), files + file(output, summary)

type modinfo is filename:seq.word, body:seq.seq.word

function getautolinks(m:midpoint, link:seq.file) set.autolink /rmbr{ this looks at the html files in link and creates autolink entries } /rmbr for autolinks0 = empty:set.autolink, sd ∈ toseq.prg.m /rmbr do if paragraphno.sd = 0 then autolinks0 /rmbr else autolinks0 + autolink( id.sym.sd, "" ) for autolinks = autolinks0, f ∈ link /rmbr do if ext.fn.f ∉ " html " then autolinks /rmbr else for autolink1 = autolinks /rmbr, p1 ∈ breakparagraph.[f] do if isempty.p1 then autolink1 /rmbr else for autolink2 = autolink1, p ∈ break(p1, " <p> " , false) /rmbr do{ assert">Function</a>"sub 1 ∉ p report":(esc.subseq(p, 1, 4))hereyX:(esc.p)" } /rmbr if subseq(p, 1, 4) ≠ " <a id = :( dq)" /rmbr ∨ " >Function</a> " sub 1 ∉ p then autolink2 /rmbr else let i = findindex(p << 4, dq sub 1)/rmbr let linkvalue = subseq(p, 4, i + 4)/rmbr let tmp = asset.[autolink(linkvalue, " ../ /nsp " + fullname.fn.f)]/rmbr ∪ autolink2,{ assert isempty.find(autolink2, linkvalue)report":(linkvalue)herey:(esc.p)/p /rmbr "+print.find(autolink2, linkvalue)+"/p /rmbr "+print.find(tmp, linkvalue),} /rmbr tmp, autolink2, autolink1, autolinks

Function unusedsymbols2(/rmbr m:midpoint /rmbr, all:boolean /rmbr, generated0:boolean /rmbr, excessExports:boolean /rmbr, ignore0:seq.word /rmbr) seq.word /rmbr let ignore = if isempty.ignore0 then " genEnum genPEG " else ignore0 let dict = for uses = empty:set.symbol, sd ∈ toseq.prg.m /rmbr do uses + sym.sd, /rmbr uses let templates = for acc = templates.m, sym ∈ toseq.dict /rmbr do if isAbstract.module.sym /rmbr ∧ isempty. getCode(templates.m, sym) then acc + symdef(sym, empty:seq.symbol, 0)/rmbr else acc, acc let roots = for acc = empty:set.symbol, sd ∈ toseq.prg.m /rmbr do if COMMAND /rmbr ∈ options.sd then acc + sym.sd /rmbr else acc, acc let a2 = closeuse( empty:set.symbol, roots, prg.m, templates, dict) let a3 = for acc = empty:set.symbol /rmbr, prg = empty:seq.symdef /rmbr, sym ∈ toseq(dict \ a2) do let b = getSymdef(prg.m, sym), /rmbr if not. isempty.b /rmbr ∧ paragraphno.b sub 1 ≠ 0 /rmbr ⊻ generated0 then next(acc + sym, prg + b sub 1)/rmbr else next(acc, prg), if all then acc /rmbr else acc /rmbr \ for arcs = empty:set.arc.symbol, sd ∈ prg /rmbr do for arcs2 = arcs /rmbr, sy ∈ toseq( asset.code.sd ∩ acc /rmbr - sym.sd) do arcs2 + arc(sym.sd, sy), /rmbr arcs2 let g = newgraph.toseq.arcs, /rmbr nodes.g \ asset. sources.g let outsyms = if excessExports then{ symbols exported from a module and only used internally to that module } /rmbr let exportedSymbols = for acc = empty:seq.symbol, alibmod ∈ libmods.m do acc + exports.alibmod, /rmbr acc for internaluse = empty:set.symbol /rmbr, externaluse = empty:set.symbol /rmbr, sd ∈ toseq.prg.m + toseq.templates.m do for internal0 = internaluse, external0 = externaluse, sy ∈ code.sd /rmbr do if module.sy = module.sym.sd then next(internal0 + sy, external0)/rmbr else next(internal0, external0 + sy), next(internal0, external0), internaluse ∩ asset.exportedSymbols \ externaluse \ a3 else a3 for acc = empty:seq.seq.word, sym ∈ toseq.outsyms /rmbr do if name.sym ∈ ignore then acc /rmbr else acc + %.sym," Unused symbols for roots :(toseq.roots) /p :( %n. sort>alpha.acc)"

function rename(renames:seq.word, name:word) word /rmbr let i = findindex(renames, name), /rmbr if i > n.renames then name else renames sub (i + 1)

function closeuse(/rmbr done:set.symbol /rmbr, toprocess:set.symbol /rmbr, prg:set.symdef /rmbr, templates:set.symdef /rmbr, dict:set.symbol /rmbr) set.symbol /rmbr let new0 = for acc = empty:seq.symbol, sym ∈ toseq.toprocess /rmbr do acc + getCode(prg, sym), /rmbr acc let new1 = for acc = empty:seq.symbol, sym ∈ toseq. asset.new0 /rmbr do let kind = kind.sym, /rmbr if kind.sym /rmbr ∈ isOrdinary /rmbr ∨ kind.sym ∈ [ kfref] then acc + sym /rmbr else acc, asset.acc \ done let new2 = requires(new1, templates, dict, true)/rmbr \ done /rmbr ∪ new1, if isempty.new2 then done /rmbr else closeuse(done ∪ toprocess, new2, prg, templates, dict)

function ⊻(a:boolean, b:boolean) boolean /rmbr if a then not.b else b

function %(a:arc.symbol) seq.word /rmbr %.tail.a + %.head.a

Module reconstructUses

use seq.modExports

use seq1.modref

use set.symbol

Export type:sym/modref

function %(a:seq.word) seq.word a

Function exportedmodref(m:midpoint) set.sym/modref /rmbr for acc = empty:set.sym/modref, md ∈ libmods.m /rmbr do for acc2 = acc, sym ∈ exports.md /rmbr do acc2 + sym/modref(sym, modname.md), /rmbr acc2, acc

type sym/modref is sym:symbol, in:modref

function >1(a:sym/modref, b:sym/modref) ordering /rmbr sym.a >1 sym.b /rmbr ∧ in.a >1 in.b

function >2(a:sym/modref, b:sym/modref) ordering sym.a >1 sym.b

function %(a:sym/modref) seq.word /rmbr %.sym.a /rmbr + %. in.a

function addtypes(exports:seq.symbol, modname:modref, prg:set.symdef) seq.symbol /rmbr{ OPTION PROFILE } /rmbr let exporttypes = for acc = empty:seq.mytype, sym ∈ exports /rmbr do acc + types.sym + resulttype.sym, /rmbr acc let usestypes = for acc = exporttypes, sd ∈ toseq.prg /rmbr do if module.sym.sd = modname then acc + types.sym.sd + resulttype.sym.sd /rmbr else acc, removeseq.acc /rmbr \ asset.[ typereal /rmbr, typeint /rmbr, typeT] for acc = empty:seq.symbol, t ∈ toseq.usestypes /rmbr do let m2 = tomodref.t, /rmbr if m2 = modname then acc /rmbr else acc + deepcopySym.t, acc

function lookupModule(m:midpoint, modname:word) modExports /rmbr for acc = (libmods.m) sub 1, md ∈ libmods.m /rmbr do if name.modname.md = modname then md else acc, /rmbr acc

function exports(m:midpoint, modr:modref) seq.symbol /rmbr let mr = lookupModule(m, name.modr), /rmbr if isSimple.modr then exports.mr /rmbr else for acc = empty:seq.symbol, sym ∈ exports.mr /rmbr do acc + replaceTsymbol(para.modr, sym), /rmbr acc

Function reconstruceUses(/rmbr m:midpoint /rmbr, modname:word /rmbr, dict:set.symbol /rmbr, exported:set.sym/modref /rmbr, olduses:seq.seq.word /rmbr) set.modref /rmbr let md = lookupModule(m, modname)/rmbr let exports = exports.md, /rmbr if isempty.exports then empty:set.modref /rmbr else{ find symbols reference in defining module including type references } /rmbr let uses5 = for uses = exports, symlist = exports, sd ∈ toseq.prg.m /rmbr do if module.sym.sd = modname.md then next(uses + code.sd, symlist + sym.sd) /rmbr else next(uses, symlist), asset(uses + addtypes(symlist, modname.md, prg.m)) { find symbols referenced in expanding templates } /rmbr let uses6 = uses5 ∪ requires(uses5, templates.m, dict, false)/rmbr let thismodule = if isAbstract.module.exports sub 1 then moduleref( " * " + modname, typeT)/rmbr else moduleref( " * " + modname) let include0 = for acc = empty:set.symbol, sym ∈ exports /rmbr do if module.sym = thismodule then acc + sym else acc, /rmbr acc, for uses = [thismodule]/rmbr, unhandled = empty:set.set.modref /rmbr, included = include0 /rmbr, symx ∈ toseq.uses6 do if isconstantorspecial.symx /rmbr ∨ name.module.symx ∈ " $for " /rmbr ∨ module.symx = thismodule /rmbr ∨ isunbound.symx then next(uses, unhandled, included + symx)/rmbr else let sym = symx, /rmbr if sym ∈ included then next(uses, unhandled, included) /rmbr else let inmod = inModule(exported - sym/modref(sym, thismodule), sym), if n.inmod = 1 then next( uses + inmod sub 1 /rmbr, unhandled /rmbr, included ∪ asset. exports(m, inmod sub 1) ) else next(uses, unhandled + inmod, included), asset. chooseUses(uses, unhandled, modname, olduses, exported)/rmbr - thismodule

function chooseUses(/rmbr uses:seq.modref /rmbr, unhandled:set.set.modref /rmbr, modname:word /rmbr, olduses:seq.seq.word /rmbr, exported:set.sym/modref /rmbr) seq.modref /rmbr{ first make sure the parameter of the uses are included in the module } /rmbr let in = for acc = empty:set.mytype, u ∈ uses /rmbr do if isSimple.u /rmbr ∨ para.u ∈ [ typeint, typeT] then acc /rmbr else acc + para.u for new = unhandled, t ∈ toseq.acc /rmbr do new + inModule(exported, deepcopySym.t), /rmbr new{ now try and resolve unhandled module sets } /rmbr for acc = empty:set.set.modref /rmbr, newuses = asset.uses /rmbr, u ∈ toseq.in do if isempty.u /rmbr ∨ not. isempty(u ∩ newuses) then{ ignore empty sets and sets with one of the modules already in uses } next(acc, newuses)/rmbr else if n.u = 1 then{ add the single modref to uses } next(acc, newuses + u sub 1)/rmbr else next(acc + u, newuses) let tmp = if not. isempty.acc then for acc2 = empty:seq.modref, x ∈ toseq.acc sub 1 /rmbr do if %.x ∈ olduses then acc2 + x else acc2, /rmbr acc2 else empty:seq.modref, if n.tmp = 1 then chooseUses( toseq.newuses + tmp sub 1 /rmbr, acc /rmbr, modname /rmbr, olduses /rmbr, exported) else if n.newuses /rmbr > n. asset.uses then chooseUses(toseq.newuses, acc, modname, olduses, exported)/rmbr else toseq.newuses

function >1(a:set.modref, b:set.modref) ordering toseq.a >1 toseq.b

function inModule(exported:set.sym/modref, sym:symbol) set.modref /rmbr let t = toseq. findelement2(exported, sym/modref(sym, internalmod)) let tmp = if not. isempty.t /rmbr ∨ isSimple.module.sym then t /rmbr else for acc2 = t, sm ∈ toseq.exported /rmbr do if replaceTsymbol(para.module.sym, sym.sm)/rmbr = sym then acc2 + sym/modref(sym, replaceT(para.module.sym, in.sm))/rmbr else acc2, acc2 for acc = empty:set.modref, e ∈ tmp /rmbr do acc + in.e, /rmbr acc

Function requires(/rmbr uses5:set.symbol /rmbr, templates:set.symdef /rmbr, dict:set.symbol /rmbr, addtemplate:boolean /rmbr) set.symbol /rmbr for acc = empty:seq.symbol, sym ∈ toseq.uses5 /rmbr do if isconstantorspecial.sym /rmbr ∨ name.module.sym ∈ " $FOR internal " /rmbr ∨ isSimple.module.sym then acc /rmbr else for acc2 = empty:seq.symbol, sd ∈ toseq.templates /rmbr do if replaceTsymbol(para.module.sym, sym.sd)/rmbr = sym then( if addtemplate then acc2 + sym.sd else acc2)/rmbr + replaceT(para.module.sym, code.sd, dict) else acc2, acc + acc2, asset.acc

function removeseq(s:seq.mytype) set.mytype /rmbr for acc = empty:set.mytype, t ∈ s /rmbr do acc + removeseq.t, /rmbr acc

function removeseq(t:mytype) mytype /rmbr if isseq.t then removeseq. parameter.t else t

Function includecomment(modtext:seq.word) int /rmbr for i = findindex(modtext, " /p " sub 1)/rmbr while i < n.modtext /rmbr ∧ modtext sub (i + 1)/rmbr ∉ " Function type function Export unbound Builtin builtin " /rmbr do findindex(modtext << i, " /p " sub 1)/rmbr + i, i

function showZ(out:seq.word) seq.word /rmbr for acc = "" , w ∈ out /rmbr do acc /rmbr + encodeword( decodeword.w /rmbr + char1. " Z " ), acc

function replaceT(with:mytype, a:seq.symbol, dict:set.symbol) seq.symbol /rmbr for acc = empty:seq.symbol, sym ∈ a /rmbr do let b = replaceTsymbol(with, sym)/rmbr let k = findelement2(dict, b), /rmbr acc + ( if isempty.k then b else k sub 1), acc

Module frontcmd.T

precedence > for >1 >2 >3 >4 >alpha

use baseTypeCheck

use file

use seq.file

use graphcode

use prettycompilerfront

use standard

use arc.symbol

use drawGraph.arc.symbol

use graph.arc.symbol

use set.arc.symbol

use set.symbol

use symbol1

use set.symdef

use drawGraph.arc.symloc

unbound compilerFront:T(seq.word, seq.file, seq.word, seq.word) midpoint

Function front:T(/rmbr input:seq.file /rmbr, output:seq.word /rmbr, pass:seq.word /rmbr, n:seq.word /rmbr, ~n:seq.word /rmbr, mods:seq.word /rmbr, ~mods:seq.word /rmbr, within:boolean /rmbr, %:seq.word /rmbr) seq.file /rmbr{ COMMAND The front /strong is a multiple-purpose command. It outputs data from various stages of the compiler. /p /rmbr One use is to determine which functions are used between modules. The usegraph of the core functions indicates there are dependencies between the modules texio, file and bits. To see the dependences, use // block front /sp+built core.libsrc mods: textio file bits format /block A graph will be displayed with the dependencies between the modules. The nodes in the graph are the procedure names. Since a name does not uniquely identify a function, hovering over the beginning of the name will pop up a more complete description beginning with the name of the function. /p /rmbr The dependence on the module bits will not be displayed. If an earlier pass of the compiler is specified like this // front  +built taubc.libsrc mods = textio file bits format pass = text /block then it will be displayed. /p /rmbr The dependence within the module textio can be seen with // front  +built taubc.libsrc mods = textio pass = text within = /block /p /rmbr To see all the functions that call functions named /em breakparagraph in the library use // front  +built taubc.libsrc n = breakparagraph pass = text out = calledby /block /p /rmbr This will list the function definitions in a package // front  +built taubc.libsrc mods = textio out = symdef /block The format is the function followed by a post order transversal of the call tree. /p /rmbr The front command takes several parameters that control which functions are considered./br /rmbr ○ /strong n a list of names of functions to include /br /rmbr ○ /strong ~n a list of names to exclude /br /rmbr ○ /strong mods a list of modules to include /br /rmbr ○ /strong ~mods a list of modules to exculde /br /rmbr ○ /strong pass The option pass determines how much processing is done before looking at the symbols. // • /strong library Only report on functions imported from libraries. /br /rmbr • /strong text Parse the input in such a way that the source code can be reconstructed./br /rmbr • /strong pass1 Output from first stage of processing. All bindings of text to symbols have been done./br /rmbr • /strong pass1a Like pass1 with Compiler options on Export statements added. /br /rmbr • /strong pass2 After some optimization /br /rmbr • /strong all Just before code generation. /block /br /rmbr ○ /strong % The option % determines the format of the output. // • /strong sym Just the symbol names /br /rmbr • /strong symdef The symbol definitions. The format is the symbol followed by a post order transversal of the call tree./br /rmbr • /strong symdefgraph For each symbol definition, the definition is presented as a call tree graph./br /rmbr • /strong calledby The option n is ignored in building a call graph. Then only the symbols that • call symbols in n directly or indirectly are included in the graph /br /rmbr • /strong calls The option n is ignored in building a call graph. Then only the symbols that • are called(directly or indirectly)from symbols in n are included in the graph./br /rmbr • /strong txt Instead of producing a SVG graph print the args of the graph./br /rmbr • /strong baseTypeCheck /br /rmbr • /strong resultCheck /block} /rmbr let cf = compilerFront:T( if isempty.pass then " pass2 " else pass, input, " * " , "" ) let out = % /rmbr let names = n /rmbr let prg = prg.cf /rmbr let ignorenames = isempty.names ∨ out ∈ [ " calls " , " calledby " ] for selected = empty:seq.symdef, root = empty:seq.symbol, sd ∈ toseq.prg /rmbr do let ss = sym.sd, /rmbr if isconstantorspecial.ss then next(selected, root)/rmbr else if isempty.mods /rmbr ∨ name.module.ss ∈ mods /rmbr ∧ (ignorenames ∨ name.ss ∈ names)/rmbr ∧ name.ss ∉ ~n /rmbr ∧ name.module.ss ∉ ~mods then next( selected + sd /rmbr, if name.ss ∈ names then root + ss else root) else next(selected, root) let txt = if out = " sym " then for txt = "" , i ∈ selected /rmbr do txt + " /p " + %.sym.i, /rmbr txt else if out = " symdef " then for txt = "" , sd1 ∈ selected /rmbr do let kk = options.sd1, /rmbr txt /rmbr + " /p " /rmbr + %.sym.sd1 /rmbr + ( if kk = NOOPTIONS then "" else" OPTIONS: :(kk)" )/rmbr + %.code.sd1, txt else if out = " symdefgraph " then for txt = "" , sd1 ∈ selected /rmbr do txt /rmbr + " /p " /rmbr + %.sym.sd1 /rmbr + drawgraph. tograph.code.sd1, txt else if out = " baseTypeCheck " then baseTypeCheck(toseq.prg, typedict.cf) /rmbr else if out = " resultCheck " then checkresults.toseq.prg /rmbr else let syms = for acc = empty:set.symbol, sd5 ∈ selected /rmbr do acc + sym.sd5, /rmbr acc let g = for acc = empty:seq.arc.symbol, sd1 ∈ selected /rmbr do for acc2 = acc /rmbr, h ∈ toseq( asset.code.sd1 ∩ syms) do if sym.sd1 = h /rmbr ∨ not.within ∧ module.sym.sd1 = module.h then acc2 /rmbr else acc2 + arc(sym.sd1, h), acc2, newgraph.acc, let g2 = if out ∈ [ " calls " , " calledby " ] then assert not. isempty(nodes.g ∩ asset.root) report" no intersection between symbols in option n and call graph " , /rmbr subgraph( g /rmbr, reachable( if out = " calledby " then complement.g else g, root) ) else g, if out = " text " then for txt = " txt " , a ∈ toseq.arcs.g /rmbr do txt /rmbr + " /br " /rmbr + %.tail.a /rmbr + %.head.a, txt else drawgraph. newgraph.toseq.arcs.g2,[ file(output, txt)]

Function transform:T(/rmbr input:seq.file /rmbr, link:seq.file /rmbr, output:seq.word /rmbr, target:seq.word /rmbr, modrename:seq.word /rmbr, bind:boolean /rmbr, reorguse:boolean /rmbr, html:seq.word /rmbr, cleanexports:boolean /rmbr, moveexports:boolean /rmbr, patternmods:seq.word /rmbr) seq.file /rmbr{ COMMAND The transform /strong cmd takes a list of input source files. For each module in the input, a pretty printed file is created in the directory <Tau>/tmp. Additional parameters allow for different variants. // transform+tests profileExample.ls helloworld.ls /br /rmbr transform+tests profileExample.ls reorguse:/br /rmbr transform  +built profileExample.libsrc taubc.libinfo bind:/br /rmbr transform  +built profileExample.libsrc taubc.libinfo bind: reorguse: /block /p /rmbr This first variant does not require the source to be semantically correct, but the syntax must be correct. It does not change the order of the paragraphs. /p /rmbr The second is like the first except that it moves the use paragraphs to the beginning of the module, removes duplicates, and sorts them./p /rmbr The third is like the first but requires correct semantics. This allows some additional transformations such as // not(a = b)/em to become // a ≠ b /em. /br /rmbr ○ target /strong overides default target directory tmp /br /rmbr ○ bind /strong Does further processing of input to bind id's to symbols./br /rmbr ○ reorguse /strong Reorganizes use clauses. If bind /em is also specified, unnecessary use clauses are removed./br /rmbr ○ link /strong A list of file names ending with /sp.html that will not be compiled but will be scanned for functions that are called by the files. Hyperlinks will be create from the location of the call to the definition in the link files. Files without a.html extenstion are ignored. /br /rmbr ○ html /strong An html file is produced with an index of modules. This option is useful for examining source code and contains for producing documentation with imbedded Tau code.This options contains one or more of the following. // • Module /strong Include modules in the table of contents. /br /rmbr • headersOnly /strong Only include the headers of exported functions in result./br /rmbr • h1 /strong include html h1 headers in table of contents /br /rmbr • h2 /strong include html h2 headers in table of contents /br /rmbr • h3 /strong include html h3 headers in table of contents /br /rmbr • h4 /strong include html h4 headers in table of contents /br /rmbr • h5 /strong include html h5 headers in table of contents /br /rmbr • h6 /strong include html h6 headers in table of contents /block /br /rmbr ○ modrename /strong List of modules to rename in form: oldname1 newname1 oldname2 newname2... /br /rmbr ○ patternmods /strong List of modules that contains patterns. /br /rmbr See // // # /nsp patterns /href Example /a /br /rmbr ○ cleanexports /strong Remove exports for exports in module or if Export is from another module add comment to indicate where it comes from./br /rmbr ○ moveexports /strong Move all exports to just after use clauses./p /rmbr The transform /keyword command treats the function genEnum as magic and will generate code in a module for enumeration types instead of creating the code by hand. // // # /nsp enum /href genEnum Example /a} /rmbr let bind1 = bind /rmbr ∨ not. isempty.link /rmbr ∨ cleanexports /rmbr ∨ moveexports let m = if bind1 then compilerFront:T( " text " , input, "" , "" ) /rmbr else empty:midpoint, transform2( m /rmbr, output /rmbr, target /rmbr, modrename /rmbr, bind1 /rmbr, reorguse /rmbr, if isempty.link then html else html + " html " /rmbr, cleanexports /rmbr, moveexports /rmbr, input /rmbr, link /rmbr, patternmods)

Function unusedsymbols:T(/rmbr input:seq.file /rmbr, all:boolean /rmbr, generated:boolean /rmbr, excessExports:boolean /rmbr, ignore:seq.word /rmbr) seq.word /rmbr{ COMMAND unusedsymbols /strong cmd analyzes code looking for unused functions. /p /rmbr It forms the function call graph for the program. /br /rmbr It then looks for any sources in the call graph that are not the entry point of the program and lists them. Any functions that are generated from type definitions are also removed. /p /rmbr Here is an example tau // tools unusedsymbols /sp+built tools.libsrc taubc.libinfo /block /p /rmbr The behavior can be modified with flags. /br /rmbr -all /strong list all unused functions--not just the roots. /br /rmbr -generated /strong The symbols generated from type definitions are included. /br /rmbr -excessExports /strong list symbols exported from a module but only used internally to that module./br /rmbr -ignore /strong Symbols with these names are not listed in the output. Default value is genEnum genPEG} /rmbr unusedsymbols2( compilerFront:T( " text " , input, "" , "" )/rmbr, all /rmbr, generated /rmbr, excessExports /rmbr, ignore)

Module graphcode

use standard

use seq.symbol

use symbol1

use arc.symloc

use graph.arc.symloc

use set.arc.symloc

use seq.symloc

use stack.symloc

Function nodeLabel(node:symloc) seq.seq.word /rmbr let t = %.sym.node /rmbr let t2 = if t sub n.t ∈ " /br " then t >> 1 else t, /rmbr[ "" /rmbr, node2text.node /rmbr, %.loc.node + t2]

Function %(symloc) seq.word " ???? "

Export type:symloc

type symloc is loc:int, sym:symbol

function =(a:symloc, b:symloc) boolean loc.a = loc.b

function >1(a:symloc, b:symloc) ordering loc.a >1 loc.b

Function tograph(s:seq.symbol) graph.arc.symloc /rmbr for acc = empty:seq.arc.symloc /rmbr, stk = empty:stack.symloc /rmbr, i ∈ arithseq(n.s, 1, 1) do let sym = s sub i /rmbr let sons = if sym = EndBlock then for stk2 = stk, sons = empty:seq.symloc, k ∈ toseq.stk /rmbr while not. isempty.stk2 /rmbr ∧ kind.sym. top.stk2 /rmbr ∉ [ kloop, kstart] /rmbr do next( pop.stk2, sons + top.stk2), /rmbr sons + top.stk2 else for stk2 = stk /rmbr, sons = empty:seq.symloc /rmbr, count = nopara.sym /rmbr, k ∈ toseq.stk while count > 0 /rmbr do let top = top.stk2, /rmbr next( pop.stk2 /rmbr, sons + top /rmbr, if kind.sym.top = kdefine then count /rmbr else count - 1), sons let newstk = pop(stk, n.sons), /rmbr let tail = symloc(i, sym), /rmbr next( for arcs = acc, sy ∈ sons do arcs + arc(tail, sy), /rmbr arcs /rmbr, push(newstk, tail) ), newgraph.acc

Function node2text(a:symloc) seq.word /rmbr let sy = sym.a /rmbr let kind = kind.sy, /rmbr if kind = kloop then" Loop: :( firstvar.sy)" /rmbr else if isspecial.kind then let t = %.sy, /rmbr if t sub n.t ∈ " /br " then t >> 1 else t else if isconst.kind /rmbr ∨ kind = klocal then %.sy /rmbr else[ name.sy]

function fixit(r:seq.word, noNT:int) seq.word /rmbr if n.r < 3 then r /rmbr else let none = merge. " .. " /rmbr for acc = "" , l2 = none, l1 = none, e ∈ r + " .. " /rmbr do if l1 ∈ " . Function usegraph(/rmbr input:seq.file /rmbr, include:seq.word /rmbr, exclude:seq.word /rmbr, order:seq.word /rmbr) seq.word /rmbr{ COMMAND PROFILE /strong usegraph graphs /em use relationship between modules in source code. /br /rmbr options: /br /rmbr exclude /strong lists the modules to ignore in the use clauses. /br /rmbr include /strong restricts the modules considered to those listed./br /rmbr order /strong finds ordering of modules so for any arc in graph, the tail occurs before the head. /br /rmbr // nograph Does not include graph in output. /block /p /rmbr Examples: // usegraph /sp+built core.libsrc // //../documentation/Ex1usegraph.html /href Result /a /br /rmbr > usegraph /sp+built core.libsrc exclude: seq standard // //../documentation/Ex2usegraph.html /href Result /a /br /rmbr > usegraph /sp+built core.libsrc include: UTF8 words standard textio exclude: seq standard // //../documentation/Ex3usegraph.html /href Result /a /br /rmbr > usegraph /sp+core UTF8.ls textio words standard encoding xxhash exclude = seq standard /block /p /rmbr /p /rmbr The last two examples give the same result. The first excludes modules from consideration and the second only includes source files of modules that should be included. } /rmbr if not. isempty.order then let allmodules = topasssymbols. breakparagraph.input for used = empty:set.modref, e ∈ allmodules /rmbr do if isAbstract.modname.e then used /rmbr else used ∪ uses.e + modname.e let backarcs = expand(toseq.used, asset.allmodules, true)/rmbr let g0 = newgraph.toseq.backarcs /rmbr let before = reverse.orderNodes(nodes.g0, arcs.g0), /rmbr let check = check(before, toseq.arcs.g0), /rmbr( if isempty.check then " Good Ordering " /rmbr else" FailedOrdering :(check)" )/rmbr + { ???? allow compound names in include such as encoding.seq.char } " /p ordering: :(before)" /rmbr + ( if " nograph " sub 1 ∈ order then "" /rmbr else for wordarcs = empty:seq.arc.word, e ∈ toseq.arcs.g0 /rmbr do if head.e = tail.e then wordarcs /rmbr else wordarcs /rmbr + arc( merge. %.tail.e /rmbr, merge. %.head.e), drawgraph( wordarcs /rmbr, asset.include /rmbr, asset.exclude) ) else let arcs = usegraph. breakparagraph.input, drawgraph( arcs /rmbr, asset.include /rmbr, asset.exclude)

function %(a:set.modref) seq.word %.toseq.a

function check(ord:seq.modref, arcs:seq.arc.modref) seq.word /rmbr{ verify ordering of modules } /rmbr for acc = "" , a ∈ arcs /rmbr do for state = "" , grp = empty:seq.modref, m ∈ ord /rmbr do if isempty.state ∧ name.m ∈ " ( " then next( " group " , grp) /rmbr else if state = " group " then if name.m ∈ " ) " then if head.a ∈ grp ∧ tail.a ∈ grp then next( " foundhead " , empty:seq.modref) /rmbr else if tail.a ∈ grp then next( " foundtail " , empty:seq.modref) /rmbr else if head.a ∈ grp then next( " problem " , empty:seq.modref) /rmbr else next( "" , empty:seq.modref) else next(state, grp + m) else if tail.a = m /rmbr ∧ isempty.state then next( " foundtail " , grp)/rmbr else if head.a = m then if state = " foundtail " then next( " foundhead " , grp) else next( " problem " , grp)/rmbr else next(state, grp), if state = " foundhead " then acc else acc + %.a, acc

" sub 1 /rmbr, result = empty:seq.arc.word /rmbr, p ∈ lib do if isempty.p then next(currentmod, result) /rmbr else if p sub 1 ∈ " module Module " then next(p sub 2, result)/rmbr else if p sub 1 ∈ " use " ∧ n.p > 1 then let m = p sub 2, /rmbr next( currentmod /rmbr, if currentmod = m ∨ currentmod ∈ " ? " then result /rmbr else result + arc(currentmod, m) ) else next(currentmod, result), result

" then moduleref( " X " + module)/rmbr else let basetype = s sub n.s /rmbr let bt = if basetype ∈ " T " then typeT /rmbr else if basetype ∈ " int " then typeint /rmbr else if basetype ∈ " real " then typereal /rmbr else let found = lookuptype(basetype, types), /rmbr if isempty.found then newtype( internalmod, basetype)/rmbr else found sub 1, if n.s = 4 then moduleref( " X " + module, bt) /rmbr else for newtype = bt /rmbr, left = s << 3 >> 1 while not. isempty.left /rmbr do let e = left sub n.left, /rmbr if e ∈ " . " do if p sub 1 ∈ " Module module " then let newmodule = passsymbols(thisModule, uses, types), /rmbr next( result1 + newmodule /rmbr, resolvetype(p, alltypes)/rmbr, empty:set.symbol /rmbr, empty:set.modref) else if p sub 1 ∈ " type " then let sym = deepcopySym. newtype(thisModule, p sub 2), /rmbr next(result1, thisModule, asset.[sym] ∪ types, uses) else if getuses ∧ p sub 1 ∈ " use " then next(result1, thisModule, types, uses + resolvetype(p, alltypes))/rmbr else next(result1, thisModule, types, uses) for alltypes1 = empty:set.symbol, m ∈ result1 /rmbr do alltypes1 ∪ defines.m, /rmbr next(result1, alltypes1), allmodules

" / " ] then encodeword(t << 2)/rmbr else dirpath.a, next( acc /rmbr + ( if lastdir = dir then "" else" + " + dir)/rmbr + name.a /rmbr + ( if lastext = ext.a then "" else" . " + ext.a)/rmbr, dir /rmbr, ext.a), acc

Function buildhelp(/rmbr input:seq.file /rmbr, target:seq.file /rmbr, shellscript:boolean /rmbr, doc:boolean /rmbr) seq.word /rmbr{ COMMAND buildhelp /strong update helpdata in module. /br /rmbr input /strong files from which to extract the help data./br /rmbr target /strong file to update help data in /br /rmbr shellscript /strong produces shell script to define commands. /br /rmbr doc /strong format for command documentation source file. } /rmbr assert shellscript /rmbr ∨ doc /rmbr ∨ not. isempty.target report" Target must be specified. " /rmbr let gram = maketable. Function tauhelp(cmd:seq.word, %:seq.word) seq.word /rmbr{ COMMAND tauhelp /strong Help documentation for commands. /br /rmbr This information is extracted from the comment in the source code for the command. function helpdata seq.helpinfo /rmbr{ This function was created using buildhelp tools.libsrc taubc webassembly transform1info.html target:+tools tauhelp.ls } /rmbr[ helpinfo( " PEGdebug " sub 1 /rmbr, " tools " sub 1 /rmbr, " (input:seq.file, steps:seq.word, notable:boolean)seq.word{COMMAND PEGdebug /strong displays a trace of running a PEG. /br-input /strong Expecting the first paragraph of input to be input and the second paragraph to be the grammar./br-steps /strong from to. Only display steps between from and to./br-notable /strong. Do not display the parse table or grammar.} " )/rmbr, helpinfo( " buildhelp " sub 1 /rmbr, " tools " sub 1 /rmbr, " (input:seq.file, target:seq.file, shellscript:boolean, doc:boolean)seq.word{COMMAND buildhelp /strong update helpdata in module. /br input /strong files from which to extract the help data./br target /strong file to update help data in /br shellscript /strong produces shell script to define commands. /br doc /strong format for command documentation source file. } " )/rmbr, helpinfo( " entrypoint " sub 1 /rmbr, " taubc " sub 1 /rmbr, " (input:seq.file, entryUses:seq.word, core:boolean)seq.byte{COMMAND entrypoint /strong For seeing the Module the compiler generates to define the entry point. /br Options:/br entryUses /strong addition use clause added to module when building entry point. /br core /strong Only show core of Module. } " )/rmbr, helpinfo( " front " sub 1 /rmbr, " tools " sub 1 /rmbr, " :T(input:seq.file, output:seq.word, pass:seq.word, n:seq.word, ~n:seq.word, mods:seq.word, ~mods:seq.word, within:boolean, %:seq.word)seq.file{COMMAND The front /strong is a multiple-purpose command. It outputs data from various stages of the compiler. /p One use is to determine which functions are used between modules. The usegraph of the core functions indicates there are dependencies between the modules texio, file and bits. To see the dependences, use // block front /sp+built core.libsrc mods: textio file bits format /block A graph will be displayed with the dependencies between the modules. The nodes in the graph are the procedure names. Since a name does not uniquely identify a function, hovering over the beginning of the name will pop up a more complete description beginning with the name of the function. /p The dependence on the module bits will not be displayed. If an earlier pass of the compiler is specified like this // front  +built taubc.libsrc mods = textio file bits format pass = text /block then it will be displayed. /p The dependence within the module textio can be seen with // front  +built taubc.libsrc mods = textio pass = text within = /block /p To see all the functions that call functions named /em breakparagraph in the library use // front  +built taubc.libsrc n = breakparagraph pass = text out = calledby /block /p This will list the function definitions in a package // front  +built taubc.libsrc mods = textio out = symdef /block The format is the function followed by a post order transversal of the call tree. /p The front command takes several parameters that control which functions are considered./br ○ /strong n a list of names of functions to include /br ○ /strong ~n a list of names to exclude /br ○ /strong mods a list of modules to include /br ○ /strong ~mods a list of modules to exculde /br ○ /strong pass The option pass determines how much processing is done before looking at the symbols. // • /strong library Only report on functions imported from libraries. /br • /strong text Parse the input in such a way that the source code can be reconstructed./br • /strong pass1 Output from first stage of processing. All bindings of text to symbols have been done./br • /strong pass1a Like pass1 with Compiler options on Export statements added. /br • /strong pass2 After some optimization /br • /strong all Just before code generation. /block /br ○ /strong % The option % determines the format of the output. // • /strong sym Just the symbol names /br • /strong symdef The symbol definitions. The format is the symbol followed by a post order transversal of the call tree./br • /strong symdefgraph For each symbol definition, the definition is presented as a call tree graph./br • /strong calledby The option n is ignored in building a call graph. Then only the symbols that • call symbols in n directly or indirectly are included in the graph /br • /strong calls The option n is ignored in building a call graph. Then only the symbols that • are called(directly or indirectly)from symbols in n are included in the graph./br • /strong txt Instead of producing a SVG graph print the args of the graph./br • /strong baseTypeCheck /br • /strong resultCheck /block} " )/rmbr, helpinfo( " makeScript " sub 1 /rmbr, " taubc " sub 1 /rmbr, " (input:seq.file, builddir:seq.word, hashes:seq.file, output:seq.word)seq.byte{COMMAND makeScript /strong creates shell script for building code./br The commands' primary is is in the shell script taubuild./br input /strong build files /br builddir /strong build directory, usually ^(dq)+built ^(dq)./br hashes /strong two files with one containing lines from the unix command shasum. The two files are compared looking for identical lines which is used to determine which files have not be changed since the last build.} " )/rmbr, helpinfo( " makebitcode " sub 1 /rmbr, " taubc " sub 1 /rmbr, " (input:seq.file, exports:seq.word, info:boolean, profile:boolean, showllvm:seq.word, entryUses:seq.word, output:seq.word)seq.file{COMMAND makebitcode /strong compiler /br Options:/br entryUses /strong addition use clause added to module when building entry point. /br profile /strong generates information for profiling /br showllvm /strong show text form of llvm code generated for the names of procedure given./br info /strong show text form of code info /br /exports list of packes to show. } " )/rmbr, helpinfo( " prettyScript " sub 1 /rmbr, " tools " sub 1 /rmbr, " (input:seq.file, builddir:seq.word, hashes:seq.file, roots:seq.word, %:seq.word)seq.word{COMMAND prettyScript /strong pretty prints /sp.bld script./br % /strong format of output. // /br pretty /strong ? /br full /strong Graph of dependences between files./br outdated /strong like full but only include outdated files in graph /br script /strong shell script for updating without the file hashes. /block /p options used for formats other than pretty./br roots /strong only include the filenames list and their descendants in graph. /br hashes /strong ? /br builddir /strong build target directory. Defaults to ^(dq)+built ^(dq)} " )/rmbr, helpinfo( " tauhelp " sub 1 /rmbr, " tools " sub 1 /rmbr, " (cmd:seq.word, %:seq.word)seq.word{COMMAND tauhelp /strong Help documentation for commands. /br This information is extracted from the comment in the source code for the command. If no option is supplied a description of the commands are printed./br cmd /strong restrict what is displayed. /br ^(dq)cmd: help1 ^(dq)will display documentation for tauhelp only and ^(dq)cmd: help1 out ^(dq)will display only the documentation of the out option of the tauhelp command. /br Options: // /strong % format of output. /br shellscript /strong creates a shell script for commands./br full /strong Full documentations of commands /br brief /strong Show extract of documentations /block} " )/rmbr, helpinfo( " transform " sub 1 /rmbr, " tools " sub 1 /rmbr, " :T(input:seq.file, link:seq.file, output:seq.word, target:seq.word, modrename:seq.word, bind:boolean, reorguse:boolean, html:seq.word, cleanexports:boolean, moveexports:boolean, patternmods:seq.word)seq.file{COMMAND The transform /strong cmd takes a list of input source files. For each module in the input, a pretty printed file is created in the directory <Tau>/tmp. Additional parameters allow for different variants. // transform+tests profileExample.ls helloworld.ls /br transform+tests profileExample.ls reorguse:/br transform  +built profileExample.libsrc taubc.libinfo bind:/br transform  +built profileExample.libsrc taubc.libinfo bind: reorguse: /block /p This first variant does not require the source to be semantically correct, but the syntax must be correct. It does not change the order of the paragraphs. /p The second is like the first except that it moves the use paragraphs to the beginning of the module, removes duplicates, and sorts them./p The third is like the first but requires correct semantics. This allows some additional transformations such as // not(a = b)/em to become // a ≠ b /em. /br ○ target /strong overides default target directory tmp /br ○ bind /strong Does further processing of input to bind id's to symbols./br ○ reorguse /strong Reorganizes use clauses. If bind /em is also specified, unnecessary use clauses are removed./br ○ link /strong A list of file names ending with /sp.html that will not be compiled but will be scanned for functions that are called by the files. Hyperlinks will be create from the location of the call to the definition in the link files. Files without a.html extenstion are ignored. /br ○ html /strong An html file is produced with an index of modules. This option is useful for examining source code and contains for producing documentation with imbedded Tau code.This options contains one or more of the following. // • Module /strong Include modules in the table of contents. /br • headersOnly /strong Only include the headers of exported functions in result./br • h1 /strong include html h1 headers in table of contents /br • h2 /strong include html h2 headers in table of contents /br • h3 /strong include html h3 headers in table of contents /br • h4 /strong include html h4 headers in table of contents /br • h5 /strong include html h5 headers in table of contents /br • h6 /strong include html h6 headers in table of contents /block /br ○ modrename /strong List of modules to rename in form: oldname1 newname1 oldname2 newname2... /br ○ patternmods /strong List of modules that contains patterns. /br See // // # /nsp patterns /href Example /a /br ○ cleanexports /strong Remove exports for exports in module or if Export is from another module add comment to indicate where it comes from./br ○ moveexports /strong Move all exports to just after use clauses./p The transform /keyword command treats the function genEnum as magic and will generate code in a module for enumeration types instead of creating the code by hand. // // # /nsp enum /href genEnum Example /a} " )/rmbr, helpinfo( " unusedsymbols " sub 1 /rmbr, " tools " sub 1 /rmbr, " :T(input:seq.file, all:boolean, generated:boolean, excessExports:boolean, ignore:seq.word)seq.word{COMMAND unusedsymbols /strong cmd analyzes code looking for unused functions. /p It forms the function call graph for the program. /br It then looks for any sources in the call graph that are not the entry point of the program and lists them. Any functions that are generated from type definitions are also removed. /p Here is an example tau // tools unusedsymbols /sp+built tools.libsrc taubc.libinfo /block /p The behavior can be modified with flags. /br-all /strong list all unused functions--not just the roots. /br-generated /strong The symbols generated from type definitions are included. /br-excessExports /strong list symbols exported from a module but only used internally to that module./br-ignore /strong Symbols with these names are not listed in the output. Default value is genEnum genPEG} " )/rmbr, helpinfo( " usegraph " sub 1 /rmbr, " tools " sub 1 /rmbr, " (input:seq.file, include:seq.word, exclude:seq.word, order:seq.word)seq.word{COMMAND PROFILE /strong usegraph graphs /em use relationship between modules in source code. /br /br options: /br exclude /strong lists the modules to ignore in the use clauses. /br include /strong restricts the modules considered to those listed./br order /strong finds ordering of modules so for any arc in graph, the tail occurs before the head. /br // nograph Does not include graph in output. /block /p Examples: // usegraph /sp+built core.libsrc // //../documentation/Ex1usegraph.html /href Result /a /br > usegraph /sp+built core.libsrc exclude: seq standard // //../documentation/Ex2usegraph.html /href Result /a /br > usegraph /sp+built core.libsrc include: UTF8 words standard textio exclude: seq standard // //../documentation/Ex3usegraph.html /href Result /a /br > usegraph /sp+core UTF8.ls textio words standard encoding xxhash exclude = seq standard /block /p /p The last two examples give the same result. The first excludes modules from consideration and the second only includes source files of modules that should be included. } " )/rmbr, helpinfo( " wasm " sub 1 /rmbr, " webassembly " sub 1 /rmbr, " (input:seq.file, Library:seq.word, exports:seq.word, output:seq.word, info:boolean, profile:boolean)seq.file{COMMAND compile to webAssembly /p Library /br exports /br output /br profile /br} " ) ]

Module prettyScript

use file

use seq1.filename

use makescript

use standard

use svg

use arc.word

use drawGraph.arc.word

use graph.arc.word

use set.arc.word

Function prettyScript(/rmbr input:seq.file /rmbr, builddir:seq.word /rmbr, hashes:seq.file /rmbr, roots:seq.word /rmbr, %:seq.word /rmbr) seq.word /rmbr{ COMMAND prettyScript /strong pretty prints /sp.bld script./br /rmbr % /strong format of output. // /br /rmbr pretty /strong ? /br /rmbr full /strong Graph of dependences between files./br /rmbr outdated /strong like full but only include outdated files in graph /br /rmbr script /strong shell script for updating without the file hashes. /block /p /rmbr options used for formats other than pretty./br /rmbr roots /strong only include the filenames list and their descendants in graph. /br /rmbr hashes /strong ? /br /rmbr builddir /strong build target directory. Defaults to"+built"} /rmbr let format = ( if isempty.% then " pretty " else %) sub 1, /rmbr if format ∈ " pretty " then pretty.input /rmbr else let txt = makeScriptCore( input /rmbr, if isempty.builddir then " +built " else builddir /rmbr, format /rmbr, hashes), if format ∈ " script " then txt /rmbr else let asfn = tofilenames.txt /rmbr for acc = empty:seq.arc.word /rmbr, tail = false /rmbr, last = asfn sub 1 /rmbr, fn ∈ asfn do next( if tail then acc /rmbr + arc( fullname.last /rmbr, fullname.fn) else acc /rmbr, not.tail /rmbr, fn) let g2 = newgraph.acc, /rmbr let g3 = if isempty.roots then g2 /rmbr else subgraph( g2 /rmbr, reachable( g2 /rmbr, fullnames. tofilenames.roots) ), drawgraph( toseq.arcs.g3 /rmbr, empty:set.word /rmbr, empty:set.word)

Function pretty(input:seq.file) seq.word /rmbr for acc = "" , l ∈ breakparagraph.input /rmbr do if subseq(l, 1, 2) = " # File " then acc /rmbr else if subseq(l, 1, 1) ∈ [ " # " , " define " ] then acc + l + " /p " /rmbr else for all = empty:seq.seq.word /rmbr, part = "" /rmbr, width = 0 /rmbr, last = l sub 1 /rmbr, w ∈ l << 1 do if width > 90 ∧ last ∉ " . Function backparse3(s:seq.symbol, ii:int, includeDefine:boolean) int /rmbr let i = ii /rmbr assert i > 0 report" back parse 1a: :(s):(stacktrace)" /rmbr let kind = kind.s sub i, /rmbr if kind = kendblock then matchblock(s, i - 1, 0) /rmbr else let i1 = if kind = kjmp then i - value.s sub i /rmbr else i for k = i1 /rmbr, j ∈ constantseq( nopara.s sub i1, 1) do backparse3(s, k - 1, includeDefine), /rmbr if includeDefine then addDefine(s, k) else k

function matchblock(s:seq.symbol, i:int, nest:int) int /rmbr let sym = s sub i /rmbr let kind = kind.sym /rmbr let newnest = if kind ∈ [ kloop, kstart] then nest - 1 /rmbr else if kind = kendblock then nest + 1 /rmbr else nest, if nest = 0 then if kind = kloop then for k = i /rmbr, j ∈ constantseq( nopara.sym, 1) do backparse3(s, k - 1, false), /rmbr k else if kind = kstart then addDefine(s, i) /rmbr else matchblock(s, i - 1, newnest) else matchblock(s, i - 1, newnest)

function addDefine(s:seq.symbol, i:int) int /rmbr if i > 1 /rmbr ∧ kind.s sub (i - 1)/rmbr = kdefine then addDefine(s, backparse3(s, i - 2, false))/rmbr else i

Function reduceCrossings(gg1:graph.arc.layernode) graph.arc.layernode /rmbr{ reduce crossing using barycenter } /rmbr if isempty.nodes.gg1 then gg1 /rmbr else let nodes = toseq.nodes.gg1 /rmbr for acc5 = empty:seq.layernode /rmbr, layerno ∈ arithseq(layer.nodes sub n.nodes - 1, 1, 2) do for ord = empty:seq.layernode /rmbr, bset = empty:seq.int /rmbr, e ∈ toseq. findelement2(nodes.gg1, layernode(0, layerno, 0)) do let preds = toseq. predecessors(gg1, e)/rmbr for sum = 0, p ∈ preds do sum + pos.p /rmbr let barycenter = 100 * sum / n.preds, /rmbr let i = abs. binarysearch(bset, barycenter), /rmbr next( subseq(ord, 1, i - 1)/rmbr + [e]/rmbr + subseq(ord, i, n.ord)/rmbr, subseq(bset, 1, i - 1)/rmbr + [barycenter]/rmbr + subseq(bset, i, n.bset) ) { assert n.nodes.gg1 /ne 13 report %.toseq.findelement2(nodes.gg1, layernode(0, 3, 0))+"ord::(ord)bary::(bset)" } /rmbr for acc6 = acc5, idx = 1, e ∈ ord /rmbr do next( if pos.e = idx then acc6 else acc6 + layernode(no.e, layer.e, idx)/rmbr, idx + 1), acc6, if isempty.acc5 /rmbr ∨ n.nodes.gg1 ≠ 13 then gg1 /rmbr else let newnodes = asset.acc5 ∪ nodes.gg1 /rmbr for newarcs = empty:seq.arc.layernode, a ∈ toseq.arcs.gg1 /rmbr do newarcs /rmbr + arc(newnodes sub no.tail.a, newnodes sub no.head.a), newgraph.newarcs + toseq.newnodes

Module orderNodes.T

use seq1.<<.T

use set.<<.T

use seq.set.<<.T

use graph.T

use set.T

use standard

unbound addscc(order:seq.<<.T, scc:seq.<<.T) seq.<<.T

unbound toarc(<<.T) T

Function orderNodes(nodes:set.<<.T, arcs:set.T) seq.<<.T /rmbr{ forms a topological order of nodes in graph using a variant of Tarjan's algorithm for finding strongly connected compoents. } /rmbr for order = empty:seq.<<.T /rmbr, orderset = empty:set.<<.T /rmbr, remaining = nodes while n.remaining > 0 /rmbr do let e = remaining sub 1 /rmbr let succ = successors(arcs, e, orderset), /rmbr if isempty.succ then next( addscc(order, [e])/rmbr, orderset + e /rmbr, subseq(remaining, 2, n.remaining) ) else let r = f44(arcs, order, orderset, e, empty:seq.<<.T, succ)/rmbr{ ???? this messes up when accscc does not add all nodes to order } /rmbr let tmp = asset(order.r << n.order), /rmbr next(order.r, orderset ∪ tmp, remaining \ tmp), order

Function successors(arcs:set.T, n:<<.T, orderset:set.<<.T) set.<<.T /rmbr{ successors of n not in orderset } /rmbr for acc = empty:set.<<.T /rmbr, e ∈ toseq. findelement2(arcs, toarc.n) do if head.e ∈ orderset then acc /rmbr else acc + head.e, acc

function f44(/rmbr arcs:set.T /rmbr, order0:seq.<<.T /rmbr, orderset0:set.<<.T /rmbr, this:<<.T /rmbr, stk0:seq.<<.T /rmbr, succ:set.<<.T /rmbr) r2.T /rmbr for order = order0 /rmbr, orderset = orderset0 /rmbr, stk = stk0 + this /rmbr, lowlink = n.stk0 + 1 /rmbr, e ∈ toseq.succ do if e ∈ orderset then next(order, orderset, stk, lowlink) /rmbr else let successors = successors(arcs, e, orderset), /rmbr if isempty.successors then next( addscc(order, [e])/rmbr, orderset + e /rmbr, stk /rmbr, lowlink) else let i = findindex(stk, e), /rmbr if i ≤ n.stk then next(order, orderset, stk, min(i, lowlink)) /rmbr else let r = f44(arcs, order, orderset, e, stk, successors), /rmbr next(order.r, orderset ∪ asset(order.r << n.order), stk.r, min(lowlink, lowlink.r)) let i = findindex(stk, this), /rmbr if lowlink = i then r2( addscc(order, stk << (i - 1))/rmbr, subseq(stk, 1, i - 1)/rmbr, lowlink) else r2(order, stk, lowlink)

type r2 is order:seq.<<.T, stk:seq.<<.T, lowlink:int

Module brandeskopf

Graph layout based on:Fast and Simple Horizontal Coordinate Assignment Ulrik Brandes and Boris Kopf, 2002

function =(a:layernode, b:layernode) boolean no.a = no.b

function type1conflicts(g:graph.arc.layernode, orgNodeCount:int) seq.arc.layernode /rmbr for layers = empty:seq.seq.layernode /rmbr, b = 1 /rmbr, idx = 1 /rmbr, e ∈ toseq.nodes.g + layernode(0, 0, 0) do if n.layers + 1 = layer.e then next(layers, b, idx + 1) /rmbr else next( layers + toseq. subseq(nodes.g, b, idx - 1)/rmbr, idx /rmbr, idx + 1) for acc0 = empty:seq.arc.layernode /rmbr, upperlayer = layers sub 1 /rmbr, currentlayer ∈ layers << 1 do{ In paper, upperlayer = L_i and currentlayer = L_(i+1) } /rmbr for acc = empty:seq.arc.layernode, k0 = 0, l = 0, node ∈ currentlayer /rmbr do let l1 = pos.node, /rmbr if node ≠ currentlayer sub n.currentlayer then next(acc, k0, l) /rmbr else if no.node ≤ orgNodeCount then { not inner segment } next(acc, k0, l) /rmbr else let p = predecessors(g, node), /rmbr if isempty.p then next(acc, k0, l) /rmbr else{ iis is upper neighbor of inner segment ending at node } /rmbr let iis = p sub 1 /rmbr let k1 = findindex(upperlayer, iis), /rmbr for acc3 = empty:seq.arc.layernode /rmbr, start ∈ subseq(currentlayer, l + 1, l1 + 1) do let k = findindex(upperlayer, start), /rmbr acc3 /rmbr + ( if k < k0 ∨ k > k1 then [arc(start, { k1 } iis)] /rmbr else empty:seq.arc.layernode), next(acc + acc3, k1, l1), next(acc0 + acc, currentlayer), acc0

function findvertarcsUL(/rmbr RtoL:boolean /rmbr, g:graph.arc.layernode /rmbr, layers2:seq.seq.layernode /rmbr, marked:set.arc.layernode /rmbr) seq.arc.layernode /rmbr{ Step 2 is to find vertical alignments. This will return arcs that will have the two nodes with the same x value. Inner arcs are prime canidates for this vertial alignment. } /rmbr for result1 = empty:seq.arc.layernode /rmbr, lastlayer = layers2 sub 1 /rmbr, currentlayer ∈ layers2 << 1 do for result2 = empty:seq.arc.layernode, r = 0, assigned = empty:seq.int, node ∈ currentlayer /rmbr do let preds = toseq. predecessors(g, node), /rmbr if n.preds > 0 then for upperidx = empty:seq.int, @e ∈ preds /rmbr do let t2 = if RtoL then n.lastlayer + 1 - pos.@e else pos.@e, /rmbr upperidx + t2 let tmp = (n.upperidx + 1) / 2, /rmbr for result3 = result2 /rmbr, r1 = r /rmbr, assigned1 = assigned /rmbr, m ∈ if tmp * 2 = n.upperidx then [tmp, tmp + 1] else[tmp] do let m2 = upperidx sub m, /rmbr if r1 < m2 /rmbr ∧ between(m2, 1, n.lastlayer)/rmbr ∧ no.node ∉ assigned1 then let newarc = arc(lastlayer sub m2, node), /rmbr if newarc ∈ marked then next(result3, m2, assigned1) /rmbr else next(result3 + newarc, m2, assigned1 + no.node) else next(result3, r1, assigned1), next(result3, r1, assigned1) else next(result2, r, assigned), next(result1 + result2, currentlayer), result1

type block is levels:seq.layernode, start:layernode, blk:seq.int, class:int

function block(levels:seq.layernode, blk:seq.int) block /rmbr block(levels, levels sub (blk sub 1), blk, 1)

function setclass(b:block, class:int) block block(levels.b, start.b, blk.b, class)

function >1(a:block, b:block) ordering /rmbr let level = levels.a /rmbr let l1 = start.a /rmbr let l2 = start.b /rmbr let diff = layer.l2 - layer.l1, /rmbr if diff = 0 then pos.l1 >1 pos.l2 /rmbr else if diff > 0 then if diff + 1 > n.blk.a then LT /rmbr else pos.level sub ((blk.a) sub (diff + 1))/rmbr >1 pos.l2 else if -diff + 1 > n.blk.b then GT /rmbr else pos.l1 >1 pos.level sub ((blk.b) sub (-diff + 1))

function %(b:block) seq.word " { :(class.b) }{ :(start.b) } :(blk.b)"

function align(/rmbr RtoL:boolean /rmbr, gin:graph.arc.layernode /rmbr, marked:set.arc.layernode /rmbr) seq.layernode /rmbr{ For providing horizontal alignment. if RtoL then alignUR else alignUL } /rmbr for layers4 = empty:seq.seq.layernode /rmbr, thislayer = empty:seq.layernode /rmbr, layerorder = empty:seq.layernode /rmbr, n2 ∈ toseq.nodes.gin + layernode(0, 0, 0) do let layerno = n.layers4 + 1, /rmbr if layer.n2 = layerno then let layer = if RtoL then [n2] + thislayer else thislayer + n2, /rmbr next(layers4, layer, layerorder) else let tmp = if RtoL then for acc1 = empty:seq.layernode, i = 1, e ∈ thislayer /rmbr do next(acc1 + layernode(no.e, layerno, i), i + 1), /rmbr acc1 else thislayer, next(layers4 + thislayer, [n2], layerorder + tmp) let level = sort>3.layerorder /rmbr let vertarcs = findvertarcsUL(RtoL, gin, layers4, marked)/rmbr for blocks = empty:seq.seq.int, all = empty:seq.int, o5 = layerorder, aa ∈ vertarcs /rmbr do for newo = o5, newblks = blocks, allx = empty:seq.int /rmbr while no.tail.aa ≠ no.newo sub 1 /rmbr do if no.newo sub 1 ∈ all then next(newo << 1, newblks, allx)/rmbr else next( newo << 1 /rmbr, newblks + [no.newo sub 1]/rmbr, allx + no.newo sub 1) for i = 1, x ∈ newblks while no.tail.aa ∉ x do i + 1, /rmbr if i > n.newblks then next( newblks + [no.tail.aa, no.head.aa]/rmbr, all + allx + [no.tail.aa, no.head.aa]/rmbr, newo) else next( subseq(newblks, 1, i - 1)/rmbr + (newblks sub i + no.head.aa)/rmbr + newblks << i /rmbr, all + allx + no.head.aa /rmbr, newo) let tmp = asset.all /rmbr for more = blocks, e ∈ toseq.nodes.gin /rmbr do if no.e ∈ tmp then more else more + [no.e]/rmbr{ assert false report %n.blocks+"/br /rmbr "+%.vertarcs+"/br /rmbr "+%.toseq(nodes.g \ asset.all)} /rmbr for classlist = empty:seq.seq.block, maxlayer = 1, classno = 0, b ∈ more /rmbr do let val = block(level, b)/rmbr for class = 1, place = 0, blks ∈ classlist /rmbr while place = 0 /rmbr do let i = binarysearch(blks, val), /rmbr if -i ≤ n.blks ∧ maxlayer < layer.start.val ∧ pos.start.val < pos.start.blks sub -i then next(class + 1, 0)/rmbr else next(class, -i), let val2 = setclass(val, class), /rmbr next( if n.classlist < class.val2 then classlist + [val2] /rmbr else let blks = classlist sub class.val2, /rmbr replace( classlist /rmbr, class.val2 /rmbr, subseq(blks, 1, place - 1)/rmbr + [val2]/rmbr + subseq(blks, place, n.blks) ) , max(layer.start.val, maxlayer)/rmbr, max(classno, class.val) ) { assert false report"HH"+%n.classlist } /rmbr for assigned0 = empty:seq.layernode, blks ∈ classlist /rmbr do for assigned = assigned0, x = { if not.RtoL then 1 else 18 } 1, b ∈ blks /rmbr do for assigned1 = assigned, node ∈ blk.b /rmbr do let l2 = layer.level sub node, /rmbr assigned1 + layernode(node, l2, x), next(assigned1, { if not.RtoL then x+1 else x-1) } x + 1), assigned, assigned0

Function assignx(gin:graph.arc.layernode, orgNodeCount:int, scaley:int) seq.layernode /rmbr{ Final step is to merge multiple layouts into one. } /rmbr let marked = asset. type1conflicts(gin, orgNodeCount)/rmbr let UL = sort>3. align(false, gin, marked)/rmbr let UR = sort>3. align(true, gin, marked)/rmbr{ assert n.UL = n.nodes.g report"assignx:(n.UL):(n.nodes.g)"+%.UL+%n.layers } /rmbr for maxlayer = empty:seq.int /rmbr, maxpos = 1 /rmbr, lastlayer1 = 1 /rmbr, e ∈ sort. align(true, gin, marked)/rmbr + layernode(0, 0, 0) do if lastlayer1 = layer.e then next(maxlayer, max(maxpos, pos.e), lastlayer1) /rmbr else next(maxlayer + maxpos, pos.e, layer.e) for acc = empty:seq.layernode /rmbr, i ∈ arithseq(n.UL, 1, 1) do let ul = UL sub i /rmbr let x = 2 * (pos.ul + maxlayer sub layer.ul + 1 - pos.UR sub i) / 2, /rmbr next(acc + layernode(no.ul, scaley * layer.ul, x)) let t = sort. align(true, gin, marked)/rmbr for change = empty:seq.layernode /rmbr, last = layernode(1, 0, 0)/rmbr, e ∈ sort.acc do if layer.e ≠ layer.last ∨ pos.e ≠ pos.last then next(change + e, e) /rmbr else next(change + layernode(no.e, layer.e, pos.e + 1), e), sort>3.change

function keylist:T(/rmbr defineTags:seq.word /rmbr, acc:seq.word /rmbr, stkinfo:stack.stkinfo /rmbr, n:int /rmbr) seq.word /rmbr let noclass = false /rmbr for pend = acc, idx = 0 /rmbr while idx < n /rmbr do let e = undertop(stkinfo, idx)/rmbr let kind = baseon.info.e /rmbr{ if kind ∈"/span"∧ noclass then next(pend, idx+1)else } /rmbr let pend2 = if isempty.pend /rmbr ∨ last.pend ∉ " /p " then pend /rmbr else if kind ∈ " /ol /ul " then pend >> 1 /rmbr else if kind ∈ " /li /div " then pend >> 1 /rmbr else pend let content = pend2 << place.e, /rmbr let other = pend2 >> n.content, /rmbr next( other + convertText:T(defineTags, stkinfo, e, def.info.e, content, noclass)/rmbr, idx + 1), pend

/function showZ:T(out:seq.word)seq.word for acc ="", w ∈ out do acc+encodeword(decodeword.w+char1."Z"), acc

function convertText:T(/rmbr defineTags:seq.word /rmbr, stkinfo2:stack.stkinfo /rmbr, e:stkinfo /rmbr, combinedDef:seq.word /rmbr, content:seq.word /rmbr, noclass:boolean /rmbr) seq.word /rmbr let defs = getAtt.tagcontent.e /rmbr + getDefines.combinedDef let einfo = info.e /rmbr for stk = empty:stack.seq.word /rmbr, ele1 = "" /rmbr, ahead ∈ extractdef(defs, " totxt " ) + " dummy " do if ahead ∈ " - " /rmbr ∨ isempty.ele1 /rmbr ∨ last.ele1 ∈ " - " then next(stk, ele1 + ahead)/rmbr else if ele1 = " ' " then next( push(stk, [ahead]), "" ) /rmbr else let bb = not. isempty(ele1 << 1)/rmbr let newstk = if bb then push(stk, extractdef(defs, ele1)) /rmbr else let ele = ele1 sub 1, /rmbr if ele ∈ " /pre " then let args = top(stk, 2), /rmbr push( pop(stk, 2), rmprefix(args sub 1, args sub 2)) else if ele ∈ " /post " then let args = top(stk, 2), /rmbr push( pop(stk, 2), rmpostfix(args sub 1, args sub 2)) else if ele ∈ " /indent " then for skip = false /rmbr, acc = " /br " + encodeword.[char.32]/rmbr, w ∈ top.stk do if w = escapeformat then next( not.skip, acc + w)/rmbr else if skip then next(skip, acc + w) /rmbr else if w ∈ " /br " then next(skip, acc + w + encodeword.[char.32])/rmbr else next(skip, acc + w) let acc1 = if acc << (n.acc - 2)/rmbr = " /br " + encodeword.[char.32] then acc >> 1 /rmbr else acc + " /br " , push( pop.stk, acc1) else if ele ∈ " /mark " then let btag = if ismark.einfo ∨ key.einfo ∈ " /link " then " // " /rmbr else[ merge( " / " + key.einfo)], if isempty. top.stk then pop.stk /rmbr else if n. top.stk = 1 /rmbr ∧ not. ismark.info. undertop(stkinfo2, 1) then stk /rmbr else push( pop.stk, btag + top.stk) else if ele ∈ " content " then push(stk, content) /rmbr else if ele ∈ " /br " then if isempty.stk ∨ top.stk ≠ " /br " then push(stk, [ele])/rmbr else push( pop.stk, escapeFormat. " /br " + " /br " ) else if ele ∈ " /p " then push(stk, [ele]) /rmbr else if ele ∈ " class " then let key = if noclass then baseon.einfo else key.einfo, /rmbr push(stk, [key]) else let result = dawsextensions:T(ele, stk), /rmbr if not. isempty.result then result /rmbr else if ele ∈ defineTags then if isempty. top.stk /rmbr ∨ ele ∈ " /id " /rmbr ∧ subseq( top.stk, 1, 2) = " auto. " then pop.stk /rmbr else if n. top.stk = 1 /rmbr ∧ (n.toseq.stk ≤ 1 /rmbr ∨ subseq((toseq.stk) sub 1, 1, 1)/rmbr ≠ " // " ) then push(stk, [ele])/rmbr else push( pop.stk, " // :( top.stk)" + ele) else push(stk, extractdef(defs, [ele])), next(newstk, [ahead]) for acc11 = "" , x ∈ toseq.stk do acc11 + x, /rmbr if acc11 << (n.acc11 - 2) = " /p /p " then acc11 >> 1 /rmbr else acc11

Module webcallconfig

use compilerfrontT.callconfig

use symbol1

Export type:callconfig

type callconfig is a:int

Function callfunc:callconfig(ctsym:symbol, typedict:typedict, stk:seq.int) seq.int /rmbr if ctsym /rmbr = symbol( internalmod /rmbr, " + " /rmbr, [ typeint, typeint]/rmbr, typeint) then[stk sub 1 + stk sub 2]/rmbr else if ctsym /rmbr = symbol( internalmod /rmbr, " * " /rmbr, [ typeint, typeint]/rmbr, typeint) then[stk sub 1 * stk sub 2]/rmbr else if ctsym /rmbr = symbol( internalmod /rmbr, " - " /rmbr, [ typeint, typeint]/rmbr, typeint) then[stk sub 1 - stk sub 2]/rmbr else if ctsym /rmbr = symbol( internalmod /rmbr, " / " /rmbr, [ typeint, typeint]/rmbr, typeint) then[stk sub 1 / stk sub 2]/rmbr else if ctsym /rmbr = symbol( internalmod /rmbr, " = " /rmbr, [ typeint, typeint]/rmbr, typeboolean)/rmbr ∨ ctsym /rmbr = symbol( internalmod /rmbr, " = " /rmbr, [ typeboolean, typeboolean]/rmbr, typeboolean) then[ if stk sub 1 = stk sub 2 then 1 else 0]/rmbr else empty:seq.int

Module makescript

Implements the makeScript command which is used by taubuild.sh.

use UTF8

use bits
